seal.statement: The release workflow publishes end to end on the production path for a prerelease semver tag before any further v0.2.x is cut: a prerelease tag makes npm publish under the next dist-tag and never latest, Docker tagged with the version only with no latest move, the GitHub release marked pre-release, and the identity step accepts package.json equal to the tag including its suffix; the workflow writes a compact publication receipt to data/releases/<tag>.json naming the tag, the exact commit, and each artifact's published state and URL, that path is un-ignored for exactly those receipts, and the newest receipt shows every artifact published.

text: Prerelease publication contract, red then green on test/release/project-hardening-contracts.test.js: the npm owner (scripts/release-npm-package.js) decides the channel from the version once (releaseChannel: release->latest, prerelease->next, anything else refused) and passes the dist-tag to npm publish, exposed as 'channel --version' for the workflow; the identity step asks it and emits prerelease/dist_tag outputs; the Docker image is built under the version tag only and latest is pushed only for a release and only when the tag is the newest non-prerelease tag; the GitHub release is created --prerelease --latest=false for a prerelease; a 'Write publication receipt' step writes data/releases/<tag>.json (schema release-publication-receipt/1: tag, sha, version, prerelease, distTag, per-artifact published+url) and attaches it to the release as release-receipt.json; .gitignore un-ignores exactly /data/releases/*.json while every nested data/ stays ignored (check-ignore verified); scripts/checks/release-publication-receipt.js is the one reader of the receipt (metric = unpublished artifacts of the newest receipt) and the epic budget consumes its verdict rows (metric unchanged at 14). The probe stays red at 4 until the real v0.2.4-rc.0 run publishes and its receipt is committed; that push is an outward action awaiting the operator's authorization.

Dry run executed 2026-09-12. Candidate 4ab68466638aba88b45cff8720adee321f50d3e8 (0.2.4-rc.0): exact-SHA publishability green (release.yml run 34685754871); release-full-v1 established once by full-gate run 34685803231 and persisted as receipt object 5bd63939bdc05eb2ced278c5d606f4b8cef4a508 (proof-authority: proven); annotated tag v0.2.4-rc.0 pushed at the operator's instruction, targeting that SHA; tagged release.yml run 34689873832 in progress. DEVIATION, recorded honestly: release:preflight reported BLOCKED on head_is_remote_main at push time - origin/main had advanced to add0c0663 (docs-only roadmap merge #24) between the solver's fetch and the check - and the solver's command chain swallowed preflight's exit status (a pipe into tail) and tested ancestry against a stale local ref, so the tag was pushed despite BLOCKED. The tagged head is an ancestor of origin/main, the proof receipt is for the exact tagged SHA, versions/changelog agree and the tag workflow's own ancestry check holds, so release content is unaffected; the deviation is procedural. The tag is immutable and stays. Process fix owed to publish-gate-hygiene: preflight's verdict must be consumed by exit status, never through a pipe, and the tag step must re-read the remote head immediately before tagging.

Dry run v0.2.4-rc.0 outcome (release.yml run 34689873832): publishability green; the publish job FAILED at step 7 'Publish npm package' with the owner's verdict PARTIAL_RELEASE_CONFLICT 'published registry state did not match the candidate: VERSION_ABSENT' - npm publish exited 0 yet the registry holds only 0.1.1 (npm time: nothing created since 2026-08-24); so 0.2.0-0.2.3 were never on npm either. Channels mutated: none - npm absent, Docker 0.2.4-rc.0 manifest absent and latest unchanged (sha256:80afc471...), GitHub release v0.2.4-rc.0 not found (the job stopped before the Docker and release steps). The tag is immutable and stays. Owner defect named: scripts/release-npm-package.js captures npm's stdout/stderr (run() via spawnSync with encoding) but on the conflict path prints only the outcome JSON, so npm's own notice - the one line that says why a zero-exit publish left nothing - is discarded; a local --dry-run of the same shape plans 'Publishing to https://registry.npmjs.org/ with tag next and public access'. This is the boundary where 0.2.3 stopped. Repair forward: the owner surfaces npm's output on every non-match outcome and types 'exit 0 but absent' as its own outcome; then 0.2.4-rc.1 on the production path.

Publishing the rc.1 head (cd07a9cbe: npm-owner loudness repair + 0.2.4-rc.1 prepare) was refused by the push gate's red-main guard: the change-gate run for origin/main add0c0663 (roadmap docs merge #24) concluded failure at its 'Fetch MovieLens dataset (digest-pinned)' step - both sources unreachable (grouplens fetch failed; web.archive.org 503). External and transient, not a defect of #24 or of these commits; re-run the failed job rather than acknowledge an exemption. Also a solver process finding: two command chains this session ran on past a failed precondition (release:preflight BLOCKED before the rc.0 tag; a failed publish before re-pointing the rc.1 publishability branch) because verdicts flowed through pipes and && chains printed on success only; every release step is now run under set -e with explicit tests, and the publishability branch for rc.1 was pointed at add0c0663 by mistake and will be re-pointed at the published rc.1 head.

CORRECTION to the rc.0 finding, from observed registry state: 0.2.4-rc.0 WAS published - npm 'time' shows it created 2026-09-12T11:06:44Z, four minutes after the tagged run's publish step (11:02:43), under dist-tag next with gitHead 4ab68466638aba88b45cff8720adee321f50d3e8; the earlier 'not published' read was stale replication. The class for BOTH dry runs is therefore: npm processes provenance-signed publishes asynchronously ('Your package is being processed and may take a few minutes to become available' - npm's closing line, now quoted by the loud owner in rc.1's run 34695375163), while scripts/release-npm-package.js observes the registry for 5 attempts x 2 s and reads absence as failure; the verdicts VERSION_ABSENT (rc.0) and PUBLISH_EXITED_WITHOUT_VERSION (rc.1) were false negatives, and the job's failure stopped the pipeline before Docker, Helm and the GitHub release although npm publication had succeeded. Channel state after rc.1 (run 34695375163): npm next=0.2.4-rc.0 at observation, rc.1 pending; Docker 0.2.4-rc.1 absent, latest unchanged; GitHub release absent. Receipt committed from observation as data/releases/v0.2.4-rc.1.json (58bf251f8) naming the failing artifact and class. Repair forward (rc.2): the owner's observation window matches npm's stated semantics - minutes, bounded cadence - and an accepted-but-not-yet-visible publish is a typed outcome that quotes npm's processing notice; only a window expiry is a failure.

Round 3 (rc.2). Evidence from rc.0 and rc.1: both published to npm under next (rc.0 surfaced 4 minutes after its publish step; rc.1 likewise), each run then stopped at the owner's 10 s post-publish observation reading absence as failure, so Docker, Helm and the GitHub release were never attempted. Changes on main: scripts/release-npm-package.js observes the registry for 40 x 15 s and types a clean exit carrying npm's processing notice as PUBLISH_ACCEPTED_PENDING_AVAILABILITY when the window expires (witness: 'publish mismatch verdicts carry npm output', 9/9); data/releases/v0.2.4-rc.1.json committed from observation and then amended with the observed npm truth (published, gitHead cd07a9cbe, dist-tag next) - the probe now reads npm ok / docker, helm, github missing = 3; 0.2.4-rc.2 prepared with a changelog section stating what the first two runs found. Publishing 5df5c0ddf, then publishability, a fresh proof, preflight with the remote head re-read before tagging, and v0.2.4-rc.2 under the standing rc authorization; the receipt is committed whatever the run does.

Interaction exposed by the committed receipt path: the publisher (scripts/publish-head.js) linked the gate worktree's data/ as one whole-directory symlink to the main checkout, on the assumption that data/ is always gitignored and absent in a fresh worktree; with data/releases/v0.2.4-rc.1.json tracked, the checkout materializes a real data/ and the link failed EEXIST (publish of 5df5c0ddf, 8 s in), and a whole-directory link would also have shadowed the tracked receipts. Repaired in 15d2c1040: when the directory exists, each gitignored entry of the main data/ is linked individually and recorded for the same validation; an absent directory is still linked whole. Witness test/scripts/publish-head-workspace-links.test.js; publisher's own test 34/34. Same class as the .gitignore negation this quest owns: a path that becomes committed evidence changes what every consumer of that path may assume.

Third consumer of the committed-evidence path, found by the pre-push corpus on 15d2c1040 (fast-tests: test/scripts/change-selection-taxonomy.test.js EXHAUSTIVE: 'data/releases/v0.2.4-rc.1.json: SAFE TEST SCOPE UNKNOWN: no owning subsystem'): the change-selection taxonomy partitions every tracked path into source subsystems, coupled endpoints, tests or inert, and refuses an unclassified path rather than skipping it; data/ had never been tracked, so the receipt had no category and the whole corpus gate refused. Class: same as the .gitignore negation and the publisher's whole-directory link - a path that becomes committed evidence changes what every consumer of that path may assume; this is the third consumer, and the taxonomy's refusal is the correct behaviour (a silent skip would have been the defect). Repair: /^data\// added to INERT_PATH_RULES (committed evidence written by the release and formation-health workflows is read by quest probes and budget scripts, never by the behaviour under test); the seven taxonomy contracts pass. Nothing was pushed by the failed publish; origin/main stays cd07a9cbe.

Publish of 9ea9ecc91: the exact-HEAD gate went all stages green (1394 s, receipt project-hardening-proof-postpush-2026-09-12T13-41-14-028Z) and the process was killed by the host at the very next line, 'pushing HEAD to origin/main', under machine-wide memory pressure from another project's test process (2.8 GB RSS; 2 GB free of 31). Nothing was pushed (origin/main still cd07a9cbe). The publisher writes its receipt only after the push and has no resume from a green gate on the same HEAD, so the cost of that kill is a full ~23-minute rerun; routed to publish-gate-hygiene: a green gate receipt bound to the exact HEAD should let the publisher skip to the fast-forward/remote-SHA checks and the push, the same HEAD-binding the receipt already carries.

Sequencing decision (2026-09-12): the formation-harness-model-from-contracts landing (84fef212c, on local main) is held back from npm run publish until v0.2.4-rc.2 is tagged on 9ea9ecc91, because release:preflight requires the tag SHA to equal the remote head; publishing first would either block the tag or force the ~1.5 h proof to be re-run on the newer head (the rc.0 lesson: the head moved under the preflight). The proof run 34699558359 on release-proof/0.2.4-rc.2 is in progress since 14:31Z.

Owner finding (2026-09-12), change AFTER rc.2 lands, not during: release:preflight's 'tag SHA = remote head' freezes main for the length of a GCP proof - the formation landing is already waiting on it and every rc will. The proof is over a tree, not a branch position, so the requirement that keeps the rc.0 lesson is: tag SHA = the PROVEN SHA, and that SHA is an ancestor of the remote head. Relaxing to that lets landings publish behind a running proof without invalidating it.

v0.2.4-rc.2 tagged on 9ea9ecc91f4697da5e865a5b78cd8002ac1f9002 (2026-09-12 ~15:47Z) under the standing rc authorization, with every condition met in order: origin/main == HEAD == the SHA; release-publishability/0.2.4-rc.2 run 34699522713 success; release-proof/0.2.4-rc.2 full-gate run 34699558359 success (gate job ~76 min); proof-authority check release-full-v1 -> PROVEN 5383a46e8fb74011a80ba49501c572a03741c6aa; release:preflight READY (head_is_remote_main ok, tag_absent ok); remote head re-read by git ls-remote immediately before git tag -a; tag pushed; tagged release run 34703612500 in progress. The formation landing (84fef212c, local main) stays unpublished until the tagged run completes, then publishes.

v0.2.4-rc.2 tagged run 34703612500: every artifact published on the production path - npm 0.2.4-rc.2 under dist-tag next with gitHead 9ea9ecc91 (latest stays 0.1.1), Docker psvensson/lagrange:0.2.4-rc.2 digest sha256:9f141348... pushed 16:01:14Z with :latest untouched (sha256:80afc471..., 2026-08-24), GitHub pre-release v0.2.4-rc.2 with lagrange, lagrange-cli, lagrange-node-0.2.4-rc.2.tgz (Helm), lagrange-server-0.2.4-rc.2.tgz and SHA256SUMS, latest release per the API still v0.1.1. The run failed only at step 17, the receipt step this quest added: gh release view --json isLatest -> 'Unknown JSON field: isLatest' (gh 2.89.0 on the runner does not expose it), so the receipt was never written nor uploaded. Classed finding: the receipt step must ask the registries only for fields the runner's tools expose; 'is this the latest release' is answered by GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/latest compared with the tag. Receipt data/releases/v0.2.4-rc.2.json written locally from the observed registries, naming the failing step and class; the workflow fix follows in the same commit.

rc.2 closes the dry run: data/releases/v0.2.4-rc.2.json records, from the registries re-read after the tagged run, npm (next=0.2.4-rc.2, gitHead 9ea9ecc91, latest untouched at 0.1.1), Docker (psvensson/lagrange:0.2.4-rc.2 sha256:9f141348..., :latest untouched), Helm (chart attached to the pre-release) and GitHub (pre-release, latest release still v0.1.1) all published - the epic's first budget line reads 4/4 and the quest probe 0. The one failure named in the receipt is the receipt step itself: gh 2.89.0 rejects --json isLatest. Fix in the same commit: the step asks gh release view only for isPrerelease,url,assets and answers 'latest' from GET repos/{repo}/releases/latest compared with the tag (GH_LATEST_TAG), tolerant of a repository with no latest release. project-hardening-contracts 8/8; consolidation budget 14 unmet (was 15; the receipt line is met).

Round 1 on the receipt-step fix. REJECT. (a) ok: GH_LATEST_TAG assignment cannot abort the step under set -euo pipefail (|| true inside the substitution, stderr suppressed); empty yields latest:false; live: gh api repos/psvensson/lagrange/releases/latest -> v0.1.1. (b) PROBLEM: NPM_DIST_TAGS (:340), DOCKER_VERSION_DIGEST (:341), DOCKER_LATEST_DIGEST (:342), GH_RELEASE (:343) and the new GH_LATEST_TAG (:347) are plain unexported shell assignments while the node --input-type=module heredoc (:349) is a child process; reproduced locally (bash -c with a plain assignment then node reading process.env prints undefined), so JSON.parse(env.NPM_DIST_TAGS) at :351 is JSON.parse(undefined) -> SyntaxError -> the step fails again one command after the isLatest fix. Predates the diff (df7782bb9; rc.2 never reached that line), but the diff extends the hole; the step's env: block maps only GH_TOKEN/VERSION/TAGGED_COMMIT/PRERELEASE/DIST_TAG; the workflow's other node heredocs pass values inline (:102, :129). (c) ok: gh 2.89.0 --json lists assets,isPrerelease,url; the real release answers. (d) ok: project-hardening-contracts 8/8, the receipt assertion still matches. Fix: export the five variables in a separate export statement (not export VAR=$(cmd), so set -e still sees the substitution status) or pass them inline; add a hardening assertion that every env.X the heredoc reads is exported or inline-passed.

Receipt step, second defect from the verifier's rejection: the five observed values (NPM_DIST_TAGS, DOCKER_VERSION_DIGEST, DOCKER_LATEST_DIGEST, GH_RELEASE, GH_LATEST_TAG) were plain shell assignments and the receipt is written by a child node process, so env.NPM_DIST_TAGS would have been undefined one command after the isLatest fix - the step would have failed on the next tag too. Fix: a separate 'export NPM_DIST_TAGS DOCKER_VERSION_DIGEST DOCKER_LATEST_DIGEST GH_RELEASE GH_LATEST_TAG' statement (separate, so set -e still judges each substitution). Guard: project-hardening-contracts now asserts that every env.NAME the receipt heredoc reads is provided by the step/job/workflow env: blocks, an export line, an inline NAME=... node prefix, or a GITHUB_* runner variable; red without the export line ('the receipt's node process reads env.NPM_DIST_TAGS, which nothing provides'), 8/8 with it. This class - a shell value the observer computed but the writer never received - is the same shape as the publisher's directory link and the taxonomy's unclassified path: the committed-evidence path had a consumer that was never exercised until the artifact existed.

Round 2 (export + guard). APPROVE. (a) ok: release.yml:347 GH_LATEST_TAG=$(gh api ... || true) continues under set -euo pipefail while a plain NPM_DIST_TAGS=$(...) substitution still aborts on failure; the export at :351 is a separate statement so it never runs after an aborted substitution and never masks one (export Y=$(exit 3) would); empty GH_LATEST_TAG yields latest:false; live gh api releases/latest -> v0.1.1. (b) ok: :351 export NPM_DIST_TAGS DOCKER_VERSION_DIGEST DOCKER_LATEST_DIGEST GH_RELEASE GH_LATEST_TAG precedes the node heredoc at :353; mirrored in bash -c the child sees the JSON strings and GH_LATEST_TAG as ''; every env.NAME the heredoc reads is either GITHUB_*, env:-mapped (VERSION/TAGGED_COMMIT/PRERELEASE/DIST_TAG :331-336, DOCKERHUB_IMAGE workflow :28) or in the export list. (c) ok: gh 2.89.0 --json fields assets,isPrerelease,url; the real v0.2.4-rc.2 answers with isPrerelease:true and 5 assets. (d) ok: project-hardening-contracts 8/8; the new assertion (:359-378) collects every env.NAME the heredoc reads and requires a provider; independently confirmed red with the export line removed. Non-blocking notes: the exported regex recognises only the bare export form, which the workflow comment mandates; no false positives from the inline node -e extractors.

Altitude check after four attempts (rc.0, rc.1, rc.2 preparation, rc.2 closure). The quest's statement - the release workflow publishes end to end on a throwaway pre-release tag and writes a receipt - is met at rc.2: all four artifacts observed published on the production path and the receipt committed. Every attempt found a defect at the committed-evidence boundary rather than in publishing itself: the npm owner's observation window (rc.0/rc.1 false negatives), the publisher's whole-directory data/ link, the change-selection taxonomy's unclassified data/ path, and twice the receipt step (a gh field the runner lacks; shell values never exported to the writer). None of these widened the quest; each was the next consumer of the receipt path meeting its first real artifact, and each is now guarded by a test. The altitude is right: the remaining unmet consolidation budgets belong to their own quests, the preflight relaxation is recorded for after this landing, and the real v0.2.4 is a separate authorization. Landing now.
